step_2_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.engine_formula_quoted: docs/math-foundations.md §1.1: "N(T) = ⌊AS · u · T⌋" with "swing timestamps t_i = i·Δ, Δ = 1/(AS·u)"; "Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time … and a cast counts when it *starts* within the window (`_schedule_shared_casts`)."
step_2_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.derivation: Stasis is a FULL self-disable: for its 2.5 s the champion cannot declare basic attacks or cast abilities. In the engine's fight model, damage over a window T is the finite-horizon renewal-reward functional Σ_{i<N(T)} R_i with N(T)=⌊AS·u·T⌋, plus casts placed on the single shared timeline. Removing 2.5 s of that timeline strictly removes attack epochs and cast starts, hence strictly lowers outgoing TDD. Illustrative sensitivity at an effective swing rate AS·u = 0.80/s over a 60 s window: ⌊0.80·60⌋ = 48 autos with no stasis vs ⌊0.80·57.5⌋ = 46 autos with one 2.5 s stasis, i.e. 2 fewer autos, before the additional loss of ability casts whose cooldowns come up inside the frozen 2.5 s. (The rate 0.80/s is an illustration, not a scenario-sourced number; the sign of the effect is rate-independent because ⌊AS·u·(T−2.5)⌋ ≤ ⌊AS·u·T⌋ for all AS·u ≥ 0.)
step_2_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.conclusion: The new value's second clause — 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' — is FALSE. Stasis changes BOTH: it grants invulnerability (durability) AND it suppresses all outgoing damage for its duration. Outgoing TDD is exactly what a stasis window costs.

step_3_is_the_old_value_supported.claim_a: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input' — consistent with step 2: because the effect is a bounded-duration full disable (2.5 s per the wiki active text), pricing it requires knowing how many seconds of the fight window it consumes. That is a scenario input, not an item property; no seconds-in-fight number exists anywhere in the cached item data.
step_3_is_the_old_value_supported.claim_b: 'item presence alone never assumes stasis' — the effect is an ACTIVE (data/items.json `active[0]` for 3157; for 2420 it is even marked 'Single use'), not a passive. Nothing in the cached data licenses assuming the active was pressed during the modeled window, and assuming it would silently subtract autos/casts from the shared timeline (step 2). Failing closed on an unpressed active is the only data-supported behavior.
step_3_is_the_old_value_supported.conclusion: Both clauses of the old value are supported by the cached wiki text and the engine's own timing formula. No contradiction found in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md.
